title: Our next opponents: Newly promoted side impress with strong defence
text:
Our next opponents: Newly promoted side impress with strong defence | Bayer04.de 
 Back 20.11.2026 - Bundesliga 
 Share Our next opponents: Newly promoted side impress with strong defence 
 SC Paderborn 07 have secured promotion to the Bundesliga for the third time in the history of the club. And now they intend to do everything within their power to avoid relegation for the first time. On Saturday, 21 November (kick-off: 15:30 CEST), the East Westphalians are hoping to take another step in that direction at the BayArena. They will be counting on the fourth-strongest defence and the highest-rated goalkeeper in Germany’s top flight to help them do so. The lowdown on our next opponents. Position
 SC Paderborn 07 are unbeaten in the league for four matches. That equals the club record set by the East Westphalians during their first Bundesliga season in 2014. SCP07 are now competing in Germany’s top flight for the third time. In each of their previous two seasons, they finished bottom of the table and were immediately relegated back to the Bundesliga 2. Now, at their third attempt, they are determined to finally secure their place in the top flight. “We’ve come to stay,” club president Thomas Sagel said before the start of the campaign. Sporting director Sebastian Lange was also full of optimism before the season began. “We want to make history,” said the man who, as the person responsible for putting together the SC Paderborn squad, wants to play his part in ensuring that everything turns out differently – and more successfully – than in the first two attempts.
 So far, so good for the newly promoted side – that much is clear after nine matchdays. Most recently, the Blue and Blacks secured a 2-2 draw at home to Eintracht Frankfurt. If Jonathan Burkardt not equalised for Eintracht in the third minute of stoppage time, SC Paderborn would be tenth in the table on twelve points. As it stands, coach Ralf Kettemann’s team are thirteenth on ten points. “After going 1-0 down, we had the game under control and deservedly turned it round,” said the head coach after the match. “In the end, there was one corner too many, which led to the 2–2 draw.”
 Nevertheless, their record so far is impressive. They have two wins, four draws and three defeats to their name. In the second round of the DFB Pokal, despite putting up a spirited fight, they suffered a last-minute 1-0 defeat against VfB Stuttgart. Should SC Paderborn remain unbeaten for a fifth consecutive match in the Bundesliga on Saturday at the BayArena, they would set a new club record – and make history early in the season.  
 „ We’ve come to stay. Paderborn president Thomas Sagel on the East Westphalian club’s Bundesliga ambitions PersonNel
 Kettemann can rely on a well-established team. Goalkeeper Nahuel Noll, on loan from TSG Hoffenheim since the summer, has immediately proved to be a major asset to his new side. In front of him, the same trio has consistently formed the back three: Jano ter Horst, Tjark Scheller and Mattes Hansen have all been in the starting line-up for all nine league matches. The full-back positions are also firmly established: Raphael Obermair plays on the left, and Laurin Curda covers the right flank. The vice-captain secured promotion to the Bundesliga for SC Paderborn with his winner in the second leg of the play-off against VfL Wolfsburg (2–1).
 In midfield, too, the roles are clearly defined: Santiago Castañeda is a first-choice central midfielder. The 22-year-old made his debut for the USA last Wednesday in a 2–0 win against Haiti and he was one of the key players for the East Westphalian side last season. The more attacking roles are filled by two new signings: former Bayern Munich player Gabriel Vidovic and Tom Baack (FC Nürnberg), who was recently preferred to Laurin Ulrich, on loan from VfB Stuttgart.
 In attack, Kettemann usually relies on Stefano Marino and Marvin Pieringer. The latter returned to Paderborn at the start of the season from relegated FC Heidenheim, having already enjoyed a very successful spell there between 2022 and 2023. Back then, the 27-year-old scored 14 goals and provided 10 assists in 26 matches for SC Paderborn. Currently, Steffen Tigges is the East Westphalians’ most dangerous forward with two goals and one assist to date. Rayan Philippe, on loan from Hamburger SV, has not yet really made his mark, having mostly come off the bench.
 He proved unbeatable at Borussia Mönchengladbach too: only two Bundesliga keepers have more clean sheets than Paderborn’s Nahuel Noll. Problems
 There are still issues up front. The Blue and Blacks have scored just eight goals in their nine games so far. Paderborn therefore have the lowest goal tally in the league, behind Schalke 04 (5) and Union Berlin (7). SC Paderborn have failed to score in five matches. The club has not yet managed to make up for the departure of Filip Bilbija, the top scorer from their promotion-winning season, to English Championship side Derby County. Although the team have yet to win a single away game, they have secured three draws and lost only once (0–3 in Dortmund). Overall, however, the attack lacks cutting edge, and their conversion rate (7 per cent) certainly leaves room for improvement.
 Performers
 SC Paderborn boast the fourth-best defence in the league. The East Westphalians have conceded just eleven goals so far – only Borussia Dortmund (7), Bayern Munich (9) and SC Freiburg (10) have better defensive records. SCP07 have kept three clean sheets so far. Nahuel Noll has played a major part in this outstanding defensive performance. According to kicker , the 23-year-old is currently the league’s highest-rated goalkeeper. Noll impresses not only on his line but also with his confident distribution of the ball. Paderborn have also hit the mark with another new signing for their defence: Jano ter Horst was relegated to the Liga 3 with Preußen Münster last season. Now, as a right-sided centre-back, the 24-year-old is exceeding all expectations with rock-solid performances.
